bull_bear.body: Highly confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'inflection point', 'value-led growth', and 'financial prudence'. Clear focus on premiumisation as a structural margin driver rather than cyclical.

bull_bear.body: 90% of power/fuel at key plants (Sitapur, Rampur) is biofuel-driven, insulating against LPG crises. The company controls raw material procurement even for outsourced bottling units, mitigating supply chain hiccups. Magic Moments vodka volume (8.6mn cases) now rivals large global vodka brands in India, signaling a structural shift to white spirits among GenZ.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend payout (%) shown alongside Net Comprehensive Income for FY2021 to FY2026: 11.8% / 15.9% / 19.6% / 15.7% / 15.5% / 20.0%, on Net Comprehensive Income of Rs. 270 / 252 / 203 / 257 / 341 / 600 Crore.
- Return ratios improved through the period: ROE 16% / 13% / 10% / 11% / 13% / 20% and ROCE 18% / 16% / 11% / 13% / 16% / 25% for FY2021 to FY2026, with ROCE defined as "LTM EBIT / Average Capital Employed (Equity + Gross Debt)".
- A net-debt chart is presented spanning Q1 FY2019 to Q1 FY2027 under the heading "Premiumization has led to higher profitability and stronger return ratios", but only two net-debt values (Rs. 771 Crore and Rs. 106 Crore) survive the extract and cannot be reliably tied to specific quarters.
- The deck states no formal dividend policy, buyback, leverage target or capital-allocation framework beyond these disclosed ratios.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Proven capability in building brands organically - entire brand portfolio developed in-house, among the few Indian companies to do so
- Leadership across multiple IMFL categories with eight brands each selling over one million cases annually
- Innovation-led product development and R&D driving continuous premium/luxury launches
- Integrated manufacturing and supply chain network across own and third-party plants
- Presence across 100+ countries providing wide global distribution reach

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economic risk (demand sensitivity) — Ongoing global uncertainties, geopolitical tensions and moderating economic growth could dent consumer sentiment and discretionary spending; any slowdown in demand could hit IMFL volume growth and financial performance. Mitigated by a diversified portfolio across categories, price points and occasions, a premiumising mix, strong distribution and a robust balance sheet.
- Inflation / input-cost risk — Volatility in prices of key raw materials - grain, ENA (Extra Neutral Alcohol), glass and packaging materials - plus potential supply-chain disruptions could raise production costs and pressure margins. Mitigated through a diversified supplier base, commodity monitoring, backward integration, regional sourcing and premiumisation-led pricing power.
- Regulatory and state policy risk — The alcobev industry is highly regulated with state-specific laws, taxation, advertising restrictions and licensing; regulatory changes or compliance lapses could disrupt operations, delay product movement and hit profitability, as illustrated by policy developments in Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra. Mitigated by diversified geographic presence and a dedicated legal/compliance team.
- Competition risk — Strong domestic and international interest in the Indian IMFL market, particularly in premium and luxury segments, could pressure market share and pricing. The Company relies on its brand portfolio, distribution network and high entry barriers to defend its position.
- Consumer preference / moderation risk — Evolving consumer preferences, rising health awareness and changing lifestyle choices - including a gradual shift towards moderation or alternative beverages - could structurally reduce demand for traditional alcoholic beverages over the long term.
- Climate change risk — Increasing environmental regulation, climate-related disruptions and sustainability expectations may affect operations, supply chains and resource availability (e.g. water, energy), requiring continued investment in energy efficiency and responsible sourcing.
- Brand equity and reputation risk — As a consumer-facing business, performance is closely tied to brand reputation and consumer trust; product quality issues, regulatory non-compliance, negative publicity or inappropriate marketing could damage brand perception across a portfolio built almost entirely through organic brand investment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Drive value-led growth by scaling the premium and luxury portfolio
- Strengthen leadership across key domestic markets
- Expand presence in white spirits (vodka), leveraging Magic Moments' category leadership through flavours, premium variants and contemporary drinking occasions
- Deepen international footprint, aiming to build globally respected Indian brands rather than merely export products
- Expand travel retail presence (visibility, activations and advocacy across international airports)
- Strengthen supply chain, capacity and backward integration - regional sourcing, PET manufacturing, glass bottle printing, malt maturation infrastructure and captive ENA capacity - to scale efficiently while maintaining quality and service reliability
- Diversify into new luxury/lifestyle categories including tequila through the D'YAVOL partnership
- Streamline corporate structure by merging Radico Spiritzs India and its seven wholly-owned step-down subsidiaries into the Company to achieve cost efficiencies and administrative simplification
- Use digital planning tools, SAP-enabled systems and data-led procurement to improve forecasting, inventory management and supply-chain efficiency
- The Company describes itself as firmly committed to shareholders through a consistent and shareholder-friendly dividend distribution policy; the Board has formalised a minimum 20% dividend payout policy while retaining flexibility to reinvest behind premiumisation, innovation and future growth. Alongside this, management has prioritised balance-sheet strengthening and debt reduction, stating the Company is on track to become debt-free in H1 FY2027.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Radico Khaitan operates an integrated manufacturing platform of ten distilleries - six in Rampur (Uttar Pradesh), one in Sitapur (Uttar Pradesh), and three in Aurangabad (Maharashtra) held through a 36% joint venture - supported by a network of 42 bottling units nationally (5 company-owned, 6 under royalty agreements, 31 under tie-up/lease contracts). The Company has dedicated glass bottle printing units at three locations to support Magic Moments Vodka's growth and its own PET bottle manufacturing facilities in Uttarakhand and Telangana. During FY2026 the Company incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary, Radico Khaitan Scotland Limited, and made a strategic 47.5% investment in D'YAVOL Spirits (India and Netherlands entities) to build internationally relevant luxury spirits brands, including a potential entry into the tequila segment. A Scheme of Amalgamation to merge Radico Spiritzs India and its seven step-down subsidiaries into the Company is pending before the NCLT. The Company's stated strategic growth pillars include Capacity Integration, Indi-Lux and Luxury Expansion, Cost and Margin Discipline, Digital and Data-led Execution, International Business and Travel Retail, Consumer Experience and Brand Advocacy, and Innovation-led Portfolio Expansion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Premiumisation is the most important structural driver for the industry; Prestige & Above portfolio (now >45% of IMFL volumes, >70% of IMFL value) is the key growth and margin driver
- Vodka and white spirits remain significantly underpenetrated versus global markets, offering substantial headroom; vodka also offers favourable category economics (shorter production cycle, lower working-capital intensity)
- Margin expansion driven by three structural factors: premiumisation mix-shift, a supportive/benign raw material (grain, ENA) cost environment, and operating leverage as scale builds
- Rising Indian consumption story - rising incomes, favourable demographics, urbanisation, digitalisation - supports long-term premiumisation and spirits demand
- Progressive regulatory reforms in key states (Uttar Pradesh composite shops/digital licensing/e-lottery, Andhra Pradesh private retail participation, Karnataka rationalised duty framework) are improving ease of doing business, transparency and compliance, supporting industry formalisation
- Cocktail culture, premium bars, casual dining and at-home social occasions are expanding consumption occasions and driving experimentation, particularly benefiting white spirits
- Travel retail and duty-free channels are becoming more relevant as Indian outbound travel expands, increasing global brand exposure
- Indian single malts and premium/luxury whiskies are strengthening credibility of Indian-made premium spirits and enabling them to compete with imported alternatives
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Radico Khaitan delivered a milestone Q4FY26 with record 19% EBITDA margins driven by a richer portfolio mix and operating leverage, crossing INR 6,000cr revenue and INR 1,000cr EBITDA. The company is pivoting to a debt-free balance sheet by H1FY27 while guiding for 125bps margin expansion in FY27, underpinned by 20% volume growth in the Prestige & Above segment and aggressive luxury brand distribution.

open.item: Super-premium and luxury portfolio revenue is expected to be close to Rs 500 crores for FY26 versus Rs 340 crores last year.
Radico will launch Maharashtra Made Liquor (MML) through its RNV joint venture and be in the market from January 2026 onwards.

open.item: Telangana collection issues have persisted for two years; management expects the entire old outstanding to be cleared within a month.
Management expects ENA and grain prices to stay stable to favorable in the near term, providing continued margin support, while remaining mindful of external volatility.

open.promised: double 1.9 mn cases (~3.8 mn cases) mn cases

open.item: Management expects to deliver 20% plus overall IMFL volume growth in FY26 with robust contribution from the prestige and above category.
Radico is on track to cross Rs 500 crores of revenue from luxury and semi-luxury brands in FY26, up from roughly Rs 350 crores last year.
Radico estimates its FY26 scotch requirement at over Rs 250 crores in value and expects significant cost advantages from the FTA duty reduction to 75%.
Morpheus Super Premium Whisky, launched in UP, will be rolled out to 10 states in the second half of FY26, covering 70% of the segment.
open.promised: 10 states in H2FY26 count of states

open.item: After Dark, currently available in 14 states, will be taken national across 24 states in the next six months.
The Spirit of Kashmyr luxury vodka, launched in UP, will be extended to 10 states in the current fiscal year with an ambition to scale the brand globally.
Non-IMFL revenue is running at Rs 400-420 crores per quarter and is expected to grow at a single-digit rate from FY26 onwards, with country liquor growing 4-5%.
The regular category, which returned to a sharp growth trajectory from Q3 of last year, is expected to sustain that momentum in the next quarters.

Management flagged the drastic Maharashtra excise/duty change but noted the state is only 4-5% of volumes, there was no pre-buy stocking in the quarter, and no material profitability impact is expected.
Advertising and sales promotion spend will stay within the targeted range of 7% to 8% of revenue.
Management expects about 100 basis points of EBITDA margin improvement in FY26, before any benefit from duty reduction, with continuous margin improvement built into the model for 3 years.
Management is confident of surpassing Rs 500 crores of luxury and semi-luxury portfolio revenue in FY26, versus Rs 340 crores achieved in FY25 (up 32%).
Net debt (about Rs 600 crores) is to be reduced by around 35% to 40% during FY26.
Regular category volumes are back and should grow 12% to 13% in FY26.
Scotch (blended malt) imports in FY26 are projected to exceed Rs 250 crores at landed price including import duties, with any duty reduction flowing through as cost saving.
